title: The octopus-push guard lets a bare git push through when the three-parent merge is already on a ref of the pushed remote
why:
Sighting (coordinator 16:40 CST Nov 14, from lane child-cites-degen's 16:40 report; the coordinator did not read the guard text; triage read no lane output; n=1): in degen, the lane's bare `git push` tripped the octopus-push guard on commit 67f96562758e, an old 3-parent merge already on origin/main; an explicit `HEAD:branch` push passed with no override. READ by triage (guard code and record, claude-settings main): decision octopus-push-refused says "A merge that a ref of the pushed remote already holds is not new, so a lane that merges in an old octopus passes". hooks/guard_merge.py `_octopus_hit` runs `git rev-list --merges --parents <source> --not --remotes=<remote>`, with remote = the push's named remote, else origin, and reads LOCAL remote-tracking refs only (no fetch). So the refusal contradicts the decision's intent if a ref of the pushed remote held 67f96562758e. VERDICT: unknown whether it is a false alarm by code; candidate causes, none confirmed: (a) the lane's local refs/remotes/origin/* did not hold the merge (stale, unfetched); (b) a bare push on a branch whose remote is not origin (listed as a not-read note in the decision: the guard reads origin while git pushes elsewhere); (c) the explicit push differed in its source or destination (a destination named like the default branch is skipped before any read). Rule: verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent. First act of a lane: read the decision octopus-push-refused and the guard's cases (hooks/test_guard.py octopus-push, tests/guard/s17973-octopus-push.py); ask the lane for its `git remote -v`, `git config branch.<name>.remote` and whether origin/main held 67f96562758e at the push; reproduce on a throwaway clone of a merge already on main, red then green. Kin: octopus-merge-push-refused (the build step).

Facts moved from that step (relayed, unverified by triage): branch octopus-push-remote-history; a test-author is on it; PR number to follow; degen merge ddc7fa405 (3-parent merge already in degen origin/main); push 1bc168055; degen PRs 746 at 18:55 and 747 about 19:07 CST (lane tg-file-title-zero); refusal text not yet read. Owner chat (relayed 19:26 CST): "can you send a subagent on this after confirming degen coordinator's local experience on this?" Stable fix 7398a1e9a skips remote-reachable merges but misses this case; #2366 built the rule.

[20:54 CST Nov 15, triage] PR #3566 ("Test the octopus-push guard on a merge the remote already holds"; branch octopus-push-remote-history; open, draft, head 3243a4494841, REST read at 20:54 CST Nov 15, pull_request_read). Consultant 20:54 CST Nov 15 (his word, unread by triage; the head sha matches his record sha 3243a44948): round 2 Sonnet PASS, record posted at 3243a44948; it lints once main is green; no reviewer from triage is needed. Red case (consultant's wording): a stale local tracking ref hides an octopus the remote holds (hooks/guard_merge.py:1030). The PR body words the same case from the other side: a stale origin/main tracking ref makes `_octopus_hit` (line 1030) refuse a push that sends no merge; 3 of 22 octopus-push cases red on dd18b05a64 (clone's own push, a linked worktree, `git -C` from another clone). Triage read only the PR body, not the diff; the body says tests only, new file tests/guard/s17974-octopus-push-remote.py, while the REST read shows 9 files changed, 390 additions, 75 deletions: the body may be stale, unchecked.

[21:02 CST Nov 15, triage] Consultant's correction 20:56 CST Nov 15 (his word, relayed by the coordinator; unread by triage): the PR #3566 body was the test-author's stale draft and is rewritten. The guard code changed (hooks/guard_merge.py, a new git_reads.py, hooks/guard.py). Guard rounds: round 1 FAIL, fix check FAIL, round 2 PASS. Cause: a stale origin/main hides that the remote already holds the octopus, so the guard refuses a push that sends no new merge. This replaces the 'tests only' reading in the 20:5x line above; triage has not re-read the PR body.
